drafts.title: Keep or improve ride comfort on broken pavement
drafts.description: Customers experience reduced harshness and a smoother ride on broken or potholed roads compared with today’s 5 Series, so long-distance and daily driving feel less fatiguing.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a user-panel and instrumented test on a defined broken-pavement route, perceived harshness (mean panel score) improves by at least 15% versus the current 5 Series baseline and seat-pan vertical acceleration RMS is reduced by at least 10% in 95% of runs.
assumptions: A current, instrumented baseline run of the latest 5 Series is available for comparison.
Vehicle mass and wheel/tire package remain within ±10% of today's baseline for fair comparison.
uncertainties: Trade-offs between ride comfort and sporty handling on some suspension setups may require tuning choices.
Perception improvements depend on consistent test conditions and representative panel composition.

drafts.title: Increase real-world electric range to meet customer expectations (realistic successor target)
drafts.description: Customers get substantially more real-world driving range on a single charge so long-distance EV trips are less constrained and range anxiety is reduced.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Real-world combined-range (EPA-equivalent or equivalent real-world driving cycle) of at least 400 miles in the most efficient powertrain/configuration, verified in third-party real-world range tests.
assumptions: Battery energy density and packaging improve modestly versus today’s 5 Series within 3–5 years (cell and pack improvements, and available vehicle architecture allow a pack sized to deliver ~400 mi).
The target applies to the most efficient configuration (aero wheels, lowest rolling-resistance tires, single-motor or most efficient dual-motor calibration).
uncertainties: Actual achievable range depends on final vehicle packaging, allowable battery size, and regulatory test procedures.
Customer desire for 600–700 miles exceeds what is realistic for a successor in this vehicle segment without large shifts in vehicle architecture or weight.

drafts.title: Make finding compatible fast chargers on trips quick and unambiguous
drafts.description: When planning or on a trip, customers can find fast chargers that work with the car quickly and understand connector compatibility and estimated availability so they aren’t slowed down or confused.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Trip-planning and charger-search results identify compatible DC fast chargers (connector type and compatibility) within 5 seconds, and in 90% of 50 representative test trips the system lists at least one compatible fast charger within 10 minutes or within 10 miles of the planned route.
assumptions: Access to up-to-date third-party charger metadata and live availability APIs is available through commercial partnerships or data providers.
Backend connectivity is available during trip planning.
uncertainties: Third-party charger data completeness and real-time availability accuracy vary by region and network.
Some chargers may require adapters or network authentication that affect usability despite being listed as 'compatible'.

drafts.title: Reduce distracting wind noise at highway speeds (above 70 mph)
drafts.description: Customers experience lower and less distracting wind noise inside the cabin when driving at highway speeds, improving long-distance comfort and perceived quality.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Measured A‑weighted interior sound pressure level at the driver's ear position is ≤68 dB(A) at 70 mph in straight-line highway conditions (and subjectively rated distraction ≤2/5 in a user panel) on 95% of test runs.
assumptions: Measurement uses a defined test protocol (driver-ear microphone position, standardized roadway and speed).
Current 5 Series baseline interior SPL at 70 mph is higher than the target and improvements are achievable with aero, sealing and trim changes.
uncertainties: Crosswind, tire choice and roof accessories (e.g., racks) can significantly affect measured noise levels.
Perceived noise depends on frequency content and may require tailored mitigation beyond overall dB reduction.

drafts.title: Lane keeping assist steers smoothly in curves without abrupt corrections
drafts.description: Customers perceive lane keeping as calm and predictable: the system follows curves and lane transitions smoothly and does not produce sudden steering inputs that surprise the driver.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a standardized multi-curve highway test at 60–70 mph, lane keeping assist produces lateral-jerk (third derivative of lateral position) under 1.0 m/s^3 in 95% of curve entries and yields a mean subjective abruptness score ≤2/5 in a user panel.
assumptions: A reproducible multi-curve test route and baseline measurements from the current 5 Series are available for comparison.
Vehicle stability and safety thresholds remain enforced; safety-critical corrections are allowed but should be signalled to the driver.
uncertainties: Edge-case scenarios (sudden lane incursions by other road users) may require stronger corrections that feel abrupt but are necessary for safety.
Fine-tuning will require iterative real-world validation across road geometries and tire/axle configurations.

drafts.title: Show charging state clearly at the charge port so it’s visible at a glance
drafts.description: Customers can tell from outside the car whether charging is in progress, complete, or a fault exists by looking at the charge-port indicator without returning to the cabin or opening an app.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: From 2 meters distance and in daylight and night conditions, observers correctly identify one of three states (charging, complete, fault) in ≥95% of observations within 2 seconds.
assumptions: Indicator design includes non-color-only cues (blinking pattern or icon) so color-blind users can distinguish states.
Mounting and visibility of the port area are not obstructed by accessories (covers, adapters).
uncertainties: Very bright sunlight angles or heavy soiling of the port area can reduce visibility.
Some regional regulations may constrain exterior indication methods.

drafts.title: Offer a clearly signalled conditional hands-off driving mode when and where legally permitted
drafts.description: Where laws and approvals allow conditional automated driving, customers can enable a hands-off driving mode that is clearly indicated, maintains driver monitoring, and provides timely takeover requests that give the driver sufficient time to resume control.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: When operating on a road where conditional automated driving is enabled, the system sustains hands-off driving for at least 5 minutes while monitoring driver engagement; upon a need for takeover the system issues clear visual and audible alerts and provides at least 10 seconds for the driver to resume control.
assumptions: Regional legal approvals and type-approval (where required) are obtained to allow conditional hands-off operation.
Driver-monitoring capabilities and support systems (maps, geofencing) are available and enabled in the region.
uncertainties: Feature availability and allowed behaviors depend on local regulations and homologation outcomes.
User expectations about takeover time vary by region and will require careful UX tuning.

drafts.title: Type approval for Level 3 automated driving (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers request that the vehicle receives type approval for Level 3 automated driving in Germany.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Regulatory type-approval is obtained from the relevant authority.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory type approval / homologation is outside product-level requirements and therefore out of scope.

drafts.title: Comply with California (CARB) emission limits across US states (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers request that the powertrain complies with CARB emission limits in all US states.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Vehicle meets CARB and applicable US emission requirements as evidenced by homologation / certification documents.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory compliance / type approval is out of scope for product feature requirements.

drafts.title: UN R155 cybersecurity type approval (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers request that the vehicle fulfils UN R155 cybersecurity type approval.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Vehicle receives UN R155 cybersecurity type approval and associated certification.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory certification is out of scope for product-level customer requirements.

drafts.title: Battery passport compliance (EU regulation request)
drafts.description: Customers request that the vehicle battery complies with the EU battery passport regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Battery passport data is available and verified according to the EU regulation at vehicle launch in applicable markets.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory compliance and reporting obligations are outside product-level requirements.

drafts.title: 800 V electrical architecture request (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the car uses an 800 V electrical architecture.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request documented: customer preference for an 800 V architecture is recorded; engineering evaluation required.
drafts.scope_reason: This is an engineering architecture request (component/architecture specification) and therefore out of scope for a customer-facing requirement. Engineering evaluation required.

drafts.title: 22 kW onboard AC charger request (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the onboard AC charger be upgraded to 22 kW.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request documented: customer preference for a 22 kW onboard AC charger is recorded; engineering evaluation required.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific onboard charger power rating is an engineering specification (out of scope for customer-facing requirements).

drafts.title: Solid-state battery cells with 400 Wh/kg request (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers request use of solid‑state cells with ~400 Wh/kg energy density.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request documented: customer preference for solid-state cells at ~400 Wh/kg is recorded; engineering/technology readiness evaluation required.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific cell chemistry and energy-density requests are engineering/technology specifications and out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Front brake disc diameter 395 mm request (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers request that the front brake discs have a diameter of 395 mm.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request documented: customer preference for 395 mm front brake discs is recorded; engineering evaluation required.
drafts.scope_reason: A specific brake-disc size is an engineering specification and out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Lidar supplier request for highway assist (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers request that highway assist uses a lidar sensor from a named supplier.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request documented: customer preference for a lidar supplier is recorded; procurement/engineering to evaluate supplier options.
drafts.scope_reason: Specifying a supplier for a sensor is an engineering/procurement decision and therefore out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
